config.notes: 4.8 as trigger: it is the stable safety-carrying tier that never trips the per-message cyber guard, so the orchestrator can read, summarize, and route security findings without disruptive mid-session model swaps; it costs less than Fable and does not draw down the capped Fable allowance on high-volume routing traffic. Stored once so a single edit moves it. If moved to claude-fable-5: orchestration and peer-agent communication quality improves (Fable's core strength), but every routing message touching coding or security content risks a per-message auto-swap to Opus, Fable burns the Max allowance about 2x faster and is capped at ~50% weekly, and security-task routing text itself can trip the guard; in that configuration all security content must be kept strictly inside the 4.8-pinned subagents so the trigger's own messages stay clean.

task_tier_rules.rationale: Design and spec framing is where capability compounds; predictably code-heavy design should start on Opus 5 to avoid paying Fable drawdown for guard-swapped output.
Opus 5 matches Fable closely on structured reasoning at half the cost and no allowance cap; escalate to Fable only when the problem is ambiguity-dominated.

task_tier_rules.surface_note: either (2026-08-26 tests: opus-spawned subagents come up as Opus 4.8, so model:opus live spawns appear to satisfy this; re-verify, and pin by full ID in agent definitions regardless)
task_tier_rules.rationale: Hard constraint: 4.8 is the stable tier that does not trip the per-message cyber guard; never execute security work on Fable or Opus 5.
With a full spec Sonnet delivers near-parity output at a fraction of the cost and parallelizes cleanly.
Roughly 3 or fewer tool calls with a specific question; any larger model is pure waste.
Sustained multi-subagent orchestration is a named Fable strength that compounds over long sessions; keep security content out of its messages to avoid guard swaps.
Navigating ambiguity is Fable's headline strength and this work is mostly prose, so it rarely trips the coding auto-swap; low volume keeps allowance impact small.
Documentation from existing source material is structured transformation Sonnet does well; escalate to Opus 5 only for architecture-narrative docs needing real synthesis.
Review compounds, but Fable auto-swaps to Opus on code content anyway, making Opus 5 the effective ceiling at lower cost; fast mode helps latency-sensitive gates.
Well-trodden patterns with clear acceptance criteria; Sonnet is the reliability floor (Haiku only for genuinely trivial single-file changes).

agent_defaults.rationale: Every task this agent runs is security work, so its default IS the security pin; the alias is nearest-only and non-compliant (resolves to Opus 5), so aegis must always be spawned via the agent-definition surface.
Offensive-security engagement lead; permanently pinned to 4.8 including attack-narrative synthesis; agent-definition surface only, alias non-compliant.
Pentest execution is guard-tripping content by definition; pinned to 4.8, agent-definition surface only, alias non-compliant.
UI and component implementation against a spec is Sonnet's sweet spot; escalate gnarly state-management or accessibility-architecture problems to opus.
API and service implementation given a spec fits Sonnet; destructive schema/migration design decisions should be escalated to opus before execution.
Test authoring, coverage passes, and bug repro are mechanical and parallelizable; escalate flaky-test root-cause hunts to opus.
Quality-gate verdicts compound; Opus 5 is the effective ceiling for code content anyway since Fable auto-swaps on it.
System design, ADRs, and trade-off framing are exactly where Fable's ambiguity and spec-framing strength compounds; low task volume keeps drawdown acceptable.
Requirements and epic breakdown are strong-reasoning prose work Opus 5 handles at half the cost; escalate genuinely ambiguous greenfield discovery to fable.
Docs and knowledge-base maintenance from existing material is structured transformation; Sonnet is the best token-to-quality tier for it.
Versioning, changelog collation, and release checklists are procedural but consequential; Sonnet is the reliability floor, Haiku acceptable for pure changelog collation sub-steps.
Lateral thinking and assumption-challenging is ambiguity work where Fable is strongest; invitation-only usage keeps volume and allowance cost minimal.

Mirrors config.trigger_model so orchestration behavior changes in one place; 4.8 keeps routing immune to guard swaps when task descriptions contain security terms; if trigger_model moves, forge-master moves with it.

notes: Surface note (updated 2026-08-26): on 2026-08-25 the opus alias was observed as Opus 5; on 2026-08-26 empirical tests showed opus-spawned subagents coming up as Opus 4.8 (harness-injected identity, consistent across 4 runs, not an independent oracle; aliases move, so re-verify). Working assumption: claude-opus-4-8 is reachable via a live Agent-tool spawn (model:opus) as well as via a sub-agent definition full ID. Pin by full ID in definitions regardless, for stability.

default_alias on aegis/slag/flux is opus; per the 2026-08-26 finding that opus spawns as Opus 4.8, spawning by that alias now appears compliant with the security constraint. Confirm before relying; pin by full ID in the sub-agent definition either way.

security_override_model is claude-opus-4-8 on all 13 agents by design: any agent handed a security/dual-use/red-team/pentest/exploit/vuln/credential task switches its executor to 4.8, enforceable only via the agent-definition full-ID surface.

Fable allowance discipline: Fable draws down the Max allowance ~2x faster than Opus and is capped at ~50% weekly. Reserve it for tiers where its ambiguity/design/orchestration strength compounds (design/spec, long orchestration, brainstorm, architect, loki). Do not route mechanical or logic-bound work to Fable.

Fable per-message auto-swap: any Fable message touching coding, cybersecurity, or biology auto-swaps to Opus per-message. Routing code-dense work through Fable often yields Opus output while consuming a Fable-shaped slot, so code-heavy tiers are assigned to Opus 5 or Sonnet directly.

trigger_model and forge-master default are intentionally identical (claude-opus-4-8) so the orchestrator tier is edited in one place; if later moved to claude-fable-5, keep all security execution inside 4.8-pinned subagents so the orchestrator's own guard-tripping message volume stays near zero.
Opus 5 fast mode is available (Opus 5 only) and fits latency-sensitive quality gates (temper) and high-throughput reasoning passes.

Destructive schema/migration changes: furnace must escalate the design decision to a capable tier and follow backup-first, manual-SQL, data-loss-warning policy before execution, regardless of its Sonnet default.

Prefer the explicit full ID (claude-opus-4-8) in sub-agent definitions for stability. The bare opus alias was Opus 5 on 2026-08-25 but observed as Opus 4.8 on 2026-08-26 (aliases move); do not assume without checking.
